title: Larkspur inference economics sprint kickoff
summary: POC scoping kickoff to define success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan and per-token cost targets. Customer wants a 4-week pilot focusing on search-assist and chat summarization; constraints: 99th percentile latency < 600ms, monthly spend cap $30k, VPC requirement for logs, SOC2 compliance. Action items and next steps agreed.
topics: Deployment mode: hosted vs dedicated vs private
next_steps: Maya to share pilot pricing deck + dedicated vs hosted cost comparison (by 2027-04-09)
Tom to spin up baseline benchmark (Llama-3-13B q4) and run 1k/sample latency/cost test (by 2027-04-14)
Priya to provide 3 canonical workloads and token distribution traces (by 2027-04-10)
Ellen and Redwood security to sync on SOC2 questionnaire + VPC onboarding doc (by 2027-04-12)
Schedule mid-pilot check-in week 2 and final demo week 4
action_items: Maya - send pilot pricing deck, cost spreadsheet, and SLA note - due 2027-04-09
Tom - provision benchmark cluster, run baseline perf w/ 1k requests, collect p50/p95/p99 and token counts - due 2027-04-14
Priya - export sample workloads (search assist logs, chat summarization examples, average token lengths) - due 2027-04-10
Ellen - confirm VPC peering window and KMS key access, send security contact - due 2027-04-12
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-04-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Tom (Redwood SE), Priya (Larkspur CTO), Devon (Larkspur ML Eng), Ellen (Platform Ops)

Summary (auto): kickoff to align on POC success metrics, workload profile, budget cap $30k/month, latency SLOs, and benchmark plan.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, uh quick intros then we'll jump into scoping, um Priya do you want to kick off with a one-liner on goals?
[00:12] Priya (Larkspur): yeah thanks Maya. Our main goal is to validate a production inference path for two features: search-assist (re-ranking plus short completion) and meeting summarization for enterprise users. We need a clear cost per 1k tokens and an SLA we can bake into product. Timeline: 4 week pilot if possible.
[00:34] Tom (Redwood): great, that's tight but doable. Quick clarifying q: when you say search-assist, what's the average prompt/response token mix? do you have apriori token histograms?
[00:46] Devon (Larkspur): rough numbers — query prompts are 20-40 tokens, responses 60-120 tokens; summaries average 400 tokens. We'll export distribution but those are the medians.
[01:05] Maya: perfect, that helps. high-level success criteria we usually suggest: economics (per-token cost target), latency (p95 or p99 SLO), quality threshold (BLEU/Rouge-ish internal eval or human checks), and integration readiness. Which of these are must-haves for Larkspur?
[01:22] Priya: must-haves are p99 under 600ms for search-assist, acceptable p95 under 2.5s for summarization, and total monthly pilot spend under $30k. Quality we'll measure with our eval set; baseline is current on-prem model equivalence.
[01:38] Tom: ok p99 600ms for short completions is doable on dedicated infra with batching tuned. We'll sketch a benchmark matrix: model variants (13B vs 33B), quantization (q4/q5), and deployment modes (hosted shared, dedicated pool, private VPC).
[01:58] Ellen: on security, we require VPC for logs and keys must be customer-managed KMS, plus SOC2 attestation. Is that supported for pilots?
[02:10] Maya: yes we can run a private deployment in a customer VPC for pilots — there's some lead time for peering and KMS setup but it's standard. We'll include SOC2 documentation and a short questionnaire.
[02:26] Priya: good. also curious about caching: we have a lot of repeated prefixes for search, is KV cache worth it?
[02:34] Tom: yes for prefix reuse KV/prefix caching can reduce per-token compute by up to ~30% depending on hit rate. If your search flows repeat queries we'll see big wins. Also batching — for search-assist we can use small batch windows (up to 32) to balance latency/cost. For summarization we can batch more aggressively since latency target is looser.
[02:58] Devon: can you throw some ballpark numbers? Our finance team wants per-1k-token estimates so they'll budget the pilot.
[03:06] Tom: rough back-of-envelope: hosted shared for 13B q4 might run around $0.00025 per token for served tokens (this includes infra amortized on multi-tenant). On dedicated with reserved capacity and aggressive batching you could see effective marginal cost near $0.00008 per token, plus storage/networking. Quantization to q4_1 and kernel tuning may reduce that further. Cache hit rates of 30% would multiply-savings — so effective per-token might drop proportionally.
[03:38] Priya: okay so at our expected volume, what does that look like monthly? say 2M prompts for search and 50k summarizations.
[03:47] Tom: quick calc: assume avg tokens per search request 120 tokens (prompt+resp), 2M req -> 240M tokens. Summaries 400 tokens *50k -> 20M tokens. Total 260M tokens. Hosted shared at $0.00025/token -> $65k/month (over your $30k cap). Dedicated at $0.00008/token -> $20.8k/month, comfortably under $30k. With 30% cache hit reduction maybe down to ~$14k. These are rough — we'll run exact runbook benchmarks.
[04:27] Maya: noted, those numbers are why most customers move to dedicated pools once they scale. We'll include a reserved capacity estimate in the deck.
[04:36] Priya: what's the benchmark plan and timeline?
[04:41] Tom: propose week 0-1: ingest workloads and sample traces, configure models (13B q4 baseline), week 2: run latency/cost benchmarks at scaled load (1k rps bursts for search, steady for summaries), week 3: tuning (batching, cache, kernel params), week 4: final demo and economics report. We'll output p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens-served, GPU utilization, and a cost per token breakdown.
[05:06] Devon: for the benchmarking infra — will we use Redwood's hosted infra or bring our own cluster?
[05:12] Tom: for speed we can run the initial benchmarks on Redwood hosted dedicated test pools; if you want private VPC rig we'll parallel-run but that adds setup time for peering.
[05:23] Ellen: peering and KMS typically need 3-5 business days from our infra team. Is that timeline compatible with week 1?
[05:29] Maya: we'll plan benchmarks on hosted first while peering is set up. No blocker.
[05:34] Priya: on the cost sheet, can you break down unit economics: infra amortization, GPU hours, egress, and caching? Our CFO wants line items.
[05:43] Tom: yes line items: GPU instance cost (hourly), inferencing kernel efficiency (tokens/sec), batching efficiency (tokens per GPU-second), KV cache savings (reduced token compute), and overhead (network, storage). We'll produce a spreadsheet where you can toggle batch size and cache hit rate to see cost sensitivity.
[06:02] Priya: what about model fallbacks for reliability — if our preferred model is unavailable how do you handle graceful degradation?
[06:08] Maya: Redwood has routing policies—auto-fallback to a compatible model variant (e.g., a smaller quantized family) and region/replica. We'll show an A/B canary plan and automatic fallback thresholds.
[06:21] Devon: in terms of data handling: we need to ensure request logs aren't stored longer than 30 days and that user PII is redacted. Can we set retention?
[06:30] Tom: yes retention windows configurable, and we support field-level redaction or in-flight tokenization. We'll include config snippets in the follow-up.
[06:40] Priya: one risk is quality regression when moving from our current on-prem tuned model to the hosted variant. How do we measure regressions?
[06:47] Tom: we'll run your eval set through both systems and compute comparative metrics; also include manual annotations on a small sample. If quality drops above your threshold we can pause rollout or adjust to a higher-capacity model.
[06:58] Maya: ok let's capture concrete acceptance criteria so the pilot has a pass/fail: 1) p99 search-assist < 600ms 2) p95 summarization < 2.5s 3) per-token effective cost for pilot <= $0.0001 (dedicated target) 4) quality parity within X% (you'll define X in deliverables) 5) successful VPC peering and KMS access
[07:26] Priya: X we'll set to 3% quality delta on our eval metrics. Good.
[07:31] Ellen: any blockers on legal/contract? We may need a short pilot MSA and an NDA addendum for logs.
[07:38] Maya: standard pilot MSA plus optional data processing agreement. I'll loop in legal and send templates.
[07:44] Devon: about benchmark signals — can you surface how batching affects p99? I've seen batching tradeoffs bump p99 even if p50 improves.
[07:52] Tom: yes will produce a curve: batch size vs p50/p95/p99 at typical arrival patterns. For search-assist we'll probably keep batch sizes small (8-16) and tight latency windows, and use micro-batching to reduce added latency.
[08:06] Priya: what about quantization risks? we've seen hallucinations change slightly when moving to q4.
[08:12] Tom: noted. part of week 3 tuning is model-internal quality checks — we'll compare q4 vs fp16 vs q5 where available. If q4 introduces unacceptable quality drift we can pick a different quantization or bump the model.
[08:25] Maya: last bit, who are the stakeholders for sign-off at Larkspur?
[08:29] Priya: CTO (me) for technical sign-off, finance for budget OK (Ellen points to CFO), product for quality sign-off (will loop in later).
[08:38] Maya: perfect. We'll deliver the pricing + benchmark plan by Friday (2027-04-09) and schedule the week 1 ingest call for Monday (2027-04-12).
[08:46] Priya: sounds good, thanks.
[08:49] Maya: ok quick recap of next steps...
[08:52] [crosstalk] Devon: thanks everyone
[08:55] End
notes: Transcript contains occasional ASR errors; timestamps approximate. References: pricing deck link (sent later), SOC2 packet link (to be provided).
